outcome: No fragment candidate adopted. Production source hashes match the accepted evolution-fusion renderer. Retain the refreshed profile, failed quality cases and sixteen ordinary comparison runs for future work; no new speed or energy improvement is claimed.
profileInterpretation: The ocean-and-sky fragment counter remains the largest recorded stage, about 3.71 ms; waves are about 1.74 ms and amortized visible-sky work about 0.96 ms. Instrumented stages can overlap, and these values are not an additive frame budget.
interpretation: Full unrolling and its reassociation/ordered-sum variants failed the unchanged-output gate. Two-way unrolling passed twelve captured states but changed average GPU time by only 0.19%. Explicit-gradient foam sample pruning failed the gate; preserving implicit samples behind SIMD-uniform conditions passed twelve states but changed average GPU time by -0.09%. Skipping empty-mask foam lighting changed 28 HDR values and three display bytes in the first scene, so it was not benchmarked. No failed quality candidate was timed for adoption.

backgroundReference.relevance: Apple discusses SIMD-group functions and fragment-shader optimizations. Experiments and conclusions above come from the recorded local tests.

limitations: One Apple M1 and the recorded settings only.
Quality-failing candidates stop at the first failed scene; they do not have completed expanded-state validation. The empty-foam lighting calm and debug cases were not reached.
Stage profiling perturbs encoder scheduling and is not a production timing comparison.
CPU timing differences varied and are not interpreted as a general benefit.
nextCandidates: Keep the original cascade loop, but investigate avoiding footprint calculations for the four bands that always use gradient sampling; the compiler may already eliminate them.
Investigate conservative procedural-cloud density bounds for skipping noise work that cannot affect clamped zero density, while preserving all arithmetic in contributing regions.
